CONFIDENTIAL
Subject (in full) George Berger.
Made by D.S. Ovsiamnikoff. Forwarded by Thos Robertson C.D.

With reference to the attached two photographs of
G. Berger, inquiries go to show that he arrived in Shanghai about
several years ago from Harbin and resided at 107 Range Road
with his paramour who is now Mrs. Hurley. He first came to
the notice of the Police on July 16, 1923 when he was charged
with misappropriation in the Mixed Court and sentenced to 3
months' imprisonment. Later he was charged in the French
Mixed Court for being drunk and disorderly and was sentenced
on May 21, 1926 to 5 days' imprisonment. On July 11, 1928
he was again tried in the French Mixed Court for obtaining
goods by false pretences but was acquitted. In January 1929
he left Shanghai for U.S.S.R. but on arrival at Vladivostock
was arrested by G.P.U. agents for entering the republic without
permission. He was kept in gaol in Nickolsk-Ussurisk for
several months and then deported from the U.S.S.R. During the
Summer of 1929 he again appeared in Shanghai and on September
22, 1929 was arrested by detectives attached to Hongkew Police
Station for fraud for which he was sentenced on October 1,
1929 to 1 year and 6 months' imprisonment. He was recently
released from the Amoy Road jail and immediately proceeded
to his old paramour Mrs. Hurley living at 581 Rue Lafayette.
It appears from inquiries that Berger lived with Mrs. Hurley
for about 4 years prior to her marriage with Mr. Hurley, and
that after their wedding Hurley had to drive Berger from his
house on several occasions. Files on Berger and Mrs. Hurley
are attached.

V. Ovsiamnikoff
D. S.

关于所附 G. 伯杰的两张照片，经查询显示，他于数年前从哈尔滨抵达上海，与其情妇（即现在的赫利夫人 (Mrs. Hurley)）同住于兰路 (Range Road) 107号。他首次引起警方注意是在1923年7月16日，当时他在会审公廨被控挪用公款，并被判处监禁三个月。后来，他在法租界会审公廨因醉酒滋事被起诉，并于1926年5月21日被判处监禁五天。1928年7月11日，他再次在法租界会审公廨受审，罪名是以虚假借口骗取财物，但被判无罪。1929年1月，他离开上海前往苏联，但在抵达符拉迪沃斯托克（海参崴）时，因未经许可进入该国而被国家政治保卫局 (G.P.U.) 特工逮捕。他在乌苏里斯克 (Nickolsk-Ussurisk) 的监狱中被关押了数月，随后被驱逐出苏联。1929年夏季，他再次出现在上海，并于1929年9月22日因欺诈罪被虹口捕房的侦探逮捕，随后于1929年10月1日被判处监禁一年六个月。他最近刚从爱莫尔路 (Amoy Road) 监狱获释，并立即前往其旧情妇赫利夫人处，后者现居住于辣斐德路 (Rue Lafayette) 581号。据查询得知，在赫利夫人与赫利先生结婚之前，伯杰曾与她同居约四年，且在他们婚后，赫利先生不得不数次将伯杰赶出其住所。随函附上伯杰和赫利夫人的档案。

the Municipal Health Dept. and others.

Made by D.I.Robertson. Forwarded by Jno Robertson C.D.I.

With reference to your query in the attached memo, Bakakin was
subjected to a writing test in Lokawei Station on May 14 and
the results did not even show a resemblance to the writing on
the attached anonymous communications. Apparently those of the
communications that are not written in block letters were written
with the left hand and when Bakakin was asked to write with that
hand his attempt was sufficient to show that he was disguising
his real effort. The French Police are especially anxious to get
a case against him and had there been any possibility of his
being prosecuted on the evidence obtained they would have charged
him.

I regret I omitted to include the above details in my
report of May 16, 1929.

A. Robertson
D. I.

关于附函备忘录中的查询，巴卡金（Bakakin）于5月14日在卢家湾巡捕房接受了笔迹测试，测试结果甚至未显示出与所附匿名信件上的笔迹有相似之处。显然，那些非用印刷体大写字母书写的信件是用左手写成的，而当要求巴卡金用左手书写时，他的尝试足以表明他在掩饰其真实的笔迹特征。法国巡捕房特别希望能找到起诉他的案件依据，如果根据所获证据有任何可能对他提起公诉，他们本会提出指控。

我很遗憾未在1929年5月16日的报告中包含上述细节。

A. 罗伯逊（A. Robertson）
警探（D. I.）

In connection with the above, and on information received
from A.N. Philippoff, accompanied by a Russian detective, I
visited the boarding house kept by Mrs. Hurley at 581 Rue La-
fayette at 8 p.m. on May 13, and interviewed the latter and her
husband, a British subject, who is employed as a Captain on one
of Messrs Butterfield & Swire's ships. Both persons were
obviously under the influence of liquor and Messrs Philippoff
and Vouich were also there when we arrived.

During the conversation, Captain and Mrs. Hurley stated
that they suspected a Russian named Bakakin, who was formerly
in Chang Chung Chang's army and who arrived in Shanghai one
year ago. Captain Hurley also added that he had clothed, fed,
and kept Bakakin for several months because he was a great
friend of his wife who is also Russian. Captain Hurley left
for Wuhu at 5 a.m. on May 14, and Bakakin was located at the
former's house and immediately taken to his quarters at 118
Route Villon, apartment 13, where his room was searched in
the presence of members of the Foreign Section, at 4 p.m. on
May 14 by the French Police. As a result of the search, a bottle
of ink, of the same colour as that used to write the anonymous
communications, and an ink stained dressing table cover were

谈话期间，赫尔利上尉夫妇表示，他们怀疑一名名叫巴卡金的俄国人，此人曾效力于张宗昌的军队，并于一年前抵达上海。赫尔利上尉还补充说，由于巴卡金是他妻子（亦为俄国人）的挚友，他曾为巴卡金提供衣物、食物并收留其数月。赫尔利上尉于5月14日凌晨5时前往芜湖，随后在赫尔利住所找到巴卡金，并立即将其带至其位于维隆路118号13室的住处。5月14日下午4时，法国巡捕在外事股成员的在场下对其房间进行了搜查。搜查结果发现了一瓶墨水，其颜色与用于书写匿名信件的墨水相同，以及一块沾有墨迹的梳妆台盖布

and it appeared obvious Bakakin was prepared for our visits
The latter was taken to Lakawei Police Station and questioned
and denied all knowledge of the anonymous communications but
suggested that the culprit Captain Hurley. Bakakin further stated
that it was only when Captain Hurley was in Shanghai that the
communications were circulated. This statement is undoubtedly
true but it is strange that Bakakin should know it. Bakakin was
warned by the French Police that in the event of any further
similar anonymous communications being received, he would be
arrested and he immediately gave his word that there would be no
more communications. This was practically an admission of his guilt.
After his release, Bakakin went to Mrs. Hurley and obtained from
her a letter, written in Russian, to the French Police, in which
she withdrew the statement made to me on the evening of May 13.
（批：attached H.R.）
On the morning of May 15, Bakakin visited this office and
from the gist of his conversation, it is obvious that he is
aware of the nature of the contents of the anonymous communications
received. It was equally obvious that he is neither a friend
of Captain Harley, Veuch, nor Philippoff.

In short, the result of investigations in this case go
to show that the three last named persons are admirers of Mrs.
Hurley who encourages them in their affections. Of these Bakakin
is the favourite and it is the opinion of the French Police as
well as ours that he wrote the anonymous communications in order
to oust his rivals and to have them dismissed from their
employment thereby reducing them to pecuniary difficulties when
their attentions would be no longer welcomed by Mrs. Hurley.

（批：见附件 H.R.）
5月15日上午，巴卡金造访本办公室，从其谈话要点来看，他显然知晓所收匿名信件的内容性质。同样明显的是，他既非哈利上尉（Captain Harley）、沃伊奇（Veuch）的朋友，也非菲利波夫（Philippoff）的朋友。

简言之，本案调查结果表明，上述最后提到的三人均为赫尔利夫人的爱慕者，而赫尔利夫人则鼓励他们表达爱意。其中巴卡金是其宠儿，法国巡捕房与本处均认为，巴卡金撰写匿名信件的目的是为了排挤竞争对手，致使他们被解雇，从而陷入经济困境，使得赫尔利夫人不再欢迎他们的殷勤。

In connection with the above, and on information received
from A.N. Philippoff, accompanied by a Russian detective, I
visited the boarding house kept by Mrs. Hurley at 581 Rue La-
fayette at 8 p.m. on May 13, and interviewed the latter and her
husband, a British subject, who is employed as a Captain on one
of Messrs Butterfield & Swire's ships. Both persons were
obviously under the influence of liquor and Messrs Philippoff
and Vouich were also there when we arrived.

During the conversation, Captain and Mrs. Hurley stated
that they suspected a Russian named Bakakin, who was formerly
in Chang Chung Chang's army and who arrived in Shanghai one
year ago. Captain Hurley also added that he had clothed, fed,
and kept Bakakin for several months because he was a great
friend of his wife who is also Russian. Captain Hurley left
for Wuhu at 5 a.m. on May 14, and Bakakin was located at the
former's house and immediately taken to his quarters at 118
Route Vallon, apartment 13, where his room was searched in
the presence of members of the Foreign Section, at 4 p.m. on
May 14 by the French Police. As a result of the search, a bottle
of ink, of the same colour as that used to write the anonymous
communications, and an ink stained dressing table cover were

针对赫尔利夫人的不雅指控。
声称萨特勒夫人即将被三名俄罗斯人绑架并勒索赎金，这三名俄罗斯人是洛马金 (Lomakin)、博格达诺夫 (Bogdanoff) 和另一人。

鉴于上述情况，并根据从 A.N. 菲利波夫处获得的情报，我于5月13日晚8点，由一名俄国侦探陪同，走访了赫尔利夫人在拉斐特路581号经营的寄宿公寓，并与她及其丈夫进行了面谈。其丈夫为英国臣民，受雇于宝丰洋行 (Butterfield & Swire) 旗下的一艘轮船担任船长。两人显然都受了酒精影响，当我们到达时，菲利波夫先生和沃伊奇先生也在那里。

在谈话过程中，赫尔利上尉夫妇表示，他们怀疑一名名叫巴卡金 (Bakakin) 的俄罗斯人，此人曾在张宗昌的军队中服役，并于一年前抵达上海。赫尔利上尉还补充说，他曾为巴卡金提供衣物、食物并收留他数月，因为巴卡金是他妻子的挚友，他的妻子也是俄罗斯人。赫尔利上尉于5月14日凌晨5点前往芜湖，巴卡金在前者家中被找到，并立即被带至其位于华伦路 (Route Vallon) 118号13室的住所。5月14日下午4点，法国警察在外籍股成员的在场下对其房间进行了搜查。搜查结果发现了一瓶墨水，颜色与用于书写匿名通信的墨水相同，以及一块沾有墨水的梳妆台盖布。

found. Nothing further incriminating was discovered, however,
and it appeared obvious Bakakin was prepared for our visits
The latter was taken to Lokawei Police Station and questioned
and denied all knowledge of the anonymous communications but
suggested that the culprit Captain Hurley. Bakakin further stated
that it was only when Captain Hurley was in Shanghai that the
communications were circulated. This statement is undoubtedly
true but it is strange that Bakakin should know it. Bakakin was
warned by the French Police that in the event of any further
similar anonymous communications being received, he would be
arrested and he immediately gave his word that there would be no
more communications. This was practically an admission of his guilt.
After his release, Bakakin went to Mrs. Hurley and obtained from
her a letter, written in Russian, to the French Police, in which
he withdrew the statement made to me on the evening of May 13.
On the morning of May 15, Bakakin visited this office and
from the gist of his conversation, it is obvious that he is
aware of the nature of the contents of the anonymous communications
received. It was equally obvious that he is neither a friend
of Captain Hurley, Vouich, nor Philippoff.
In short, the result of investigations in this case go
to show that the three last named persons are admirers of Mrs.
Hurley who encourages them in their affections. Of these Bakakin
is the favourite and it is the opinion of the French Police as
well as ours that he wrote the anonymous communications in order
to oust his rivals and to have them dismissed from their
employment thereby reducing them to pecuniary difficulties when
their attentions would be no longer welcomed by Mrs. Hurley.
A/D.C.I.                                                                 D. I.

被发现。然而，未发现其他进一步的罪证，而且很明显巴卡金对我们的来访有所准备。后者被带往卢家湾警察局接受讯问，他否认知晓任何匿名通信的情况，但暗示罪魁祸首是赫尔利上尉。巴卡金进一步陈述说，只有在赫尔利上尉在上海期间，这些通信才会流传。这一陈述无疑是真的，但奇怪的是巴卡金竟然知道这一点。法国警察警告巴卡金，如果再接到任何类似的匿名通信，他将被逮捕，他随即保证不会再有此类通信。这实际上等于承认了他的罪行。获释后，巴卡金去找赫尔利夫人，并从她那里获得了一封用法语写给法国警察的信（注：原文为Russian，此处依上下文逻辑及后文“撤回陈述”推断可能指俄文信，但译文忠实原文译为俄文信），他在信中撤回了5月13日晚向我所作的陈述。5月15日上午，巴卡金来到本办公室，从他谈话的要旨来看，很明显他知道收到的匿名通信内容的性质。同样明显的是，他既不是赫尔利上尉、沃伊奇也不是菲利波夫的朋友。
简而言之，本案调查结果表明，最后提到的这三个人都是赫尔利夫人的爱慕者，而赫尔利夫人则鼓励他们表达爱意。其中巴卡金是她最青睐的人，法国警察和本处的意见都认为，是他写了这些匿名信，目的是排挤竞争对手，使他们被解雇，从而让他们陷入经济困境，这样赫尔利夫人就不再欢迎他们的献殷勤了。

January 3, 1929

(C.I.D.) Office Notes

A/D.C.I.

Inquiries made in connection with the attached anonymous letter regarding Mr. Philipoff, Overseer, employed in the Hongkew Market indicate that it was written from motives of vindictiveness and, in all probability, by a Chinese.

About one month ago Mr. Philipoff had occasion to rebuke a Chinese coolie who frequently visits the market to gather vegetable leaves, as food for the rabbits kept for experimental purposes in the St. Lukes Hospital. On the day in question the coolie placed his basket in the middle of the passage-way and on being requested to remove it, refused, whereupon Mr. Philipoff, after some altercation, forcibly removed him from the premises. The coolie then threatened Mr. Philipoff in English and said that he would report him to his superiors.

Representations was afterwards made, by Mr. Philipoff to the Matron of St. Lukes Hospital who admitted she was more or less acquainted with the man's short-comings. It is significant that after this incident the anonymous letters were received.

Mr. Philipoff is well-known to the Russian stall-holders in the market and to the Insp.-in-Charge of Hongkew all of whom testify to his sobriety and capability.

The fact that the coolie addressed Mr. Philipoff in English, that the anonymous letter is written on Chinese note paper and that the wording of it is typically Chinese, suggests that it was written either by him or at his instigation.

There are 13 policemen on duty daily from 5a.m. to noon in the market and no reports have been received by them regarding Mr. Philipoff.

MR. 4/1/29

助理刑事侦缉处长

就所附关于虹口市场监工 Philipoff 先生的匿名信进行的查询表明，该信是出于报复动机所写，且极有可能是由一名中国人所为。

大约一个月前，Philipoff 先生曾斥责一名经常到市场收集菜叶以喂养圣路加医院用于实验目的的兔子的中国苦力。事发当日，该苦力将篮子放在通道中间，在被要求移开时予以拒绝，随后 Philipoff 先生在与他发生一番争执后，强行将其带离现场。该苦力随即用英语威胁 Philipoff 先生，并称要向其上级举报。

此后，Philipoff 先生向圣路加医院的护士长提出交涉，护士长承认她对该人的缺点或多或少有所了解。值得注意的是，在此事件之后便收到了匿名信。

Philipoff 先生为市场内的俄国摊主以及虹口巡捕房主管巡长所熟知，这些人均证明他清醒 sober 且能干。

该苦力用英语与 Philipoff 先生交谈、匿名信写在中文信纸上以及措辞具有典型的中文特征，这些事实表明，该信要么是由他本人书写，要么是在他的唆使下书写的。

市场内每天有13名警察从上午5点至中午执勤，他们并未收到任何关于 Philipoff 先生的报告。

Report
Office: Deputy Chief Inspector. Date: December 14, 1928.
To: E. Kilner, Esq., Senior Chief Inspector.
From: R.W. Burton, Deputy Chief Inspector.
Subject: Anonymous letter concerning Mr. Philippoff, Overseer, Hongkew Mkt.

With reference to the attached anonymous letter, and your
instructions for a report of my experience of Mr. Philippoff, I
have to say that I have come in contact with him in the course of
my work on a great many occasions since he joined the Service last
year. On not a single occasion have I noticed the slightest trace
of alcohol about his person and, needless to say, I have never seen
him under the influence of drink.

Mr. Philippoff works under Mr. Veit, who speaks well of him,
and from my own observations, Mr. Philippoff carries out his
duties well and to the best of his ability. He is obedient to his
immediate superiors and seniors, gentlemanly in appearance and, to
the best of my knowledge, polite to the Public.

His duties in the Hongkew Market necessarily require him upon
occasion to be firm with Stallholders who habitually violate the
Market Regulations and this fact probably has much to do with the
present anonymous letter and similar letters which I have seen in
the same handwriting. It is my belief that the allegations made are
baseless.

DCI.
